# BIM-Based Modular Housing System Using Thin-Wall Channel Steel

## Overview

The present disclosure presents a Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based modular housing system constructed with thin-wall channel steel. The system comprises a comprehensive set of structural components, including foundations, columns, beams, walls, a roof plate, doors, and windows. These elements work together to form a cohesive, prefabricated housing solution that leverages the precision and efficiency of BIM technology.

## Structural Components and Materials

The columns and transverse beams are constructed using inward-flanging C-section steel. Alternatively, they may employ combined square steel, which is formed by oppositely buckling two symmetric inward-flanging C-section steel members together. This configuration provides enhanced structural integrity while maintaining the lightweight characteristics inherent to thin-wall steel construction.

## Connection System

Various structural elements—including columns, foundations, beams, and supports—are joined together through a versatile connector system. This system utilizes three primary types of connectors:

- **Base connectors**, which anchor and link foundational elements
- **Butting connectors**, which join components in an end-to-end configuration
- **Crossed connectors**, which enable intersecting connections between structural members

## Joint Design and Functionality

The joints are engineered with webs that deliver high structural strength, enabling them to function effectively as standardized connectors throughout the system. These joints incorporate relief holes, which facilitate an internal-external nesting effect in conjunction with the inward flanges of the C-section steel. This interlocking arrangement ensures a secure and precise fit between components.

Furthermore, a positioning groove located on the exterior of the joint nests with the C-section steel in a concavo-convex (interlocking) manner. This connection is then secured by a steel strip, which fastens the assembly firmly in place. Together, these features achieve the dual effects of reliable fastening and effective slippage prevention, ensuring the overall stability and durability of the modular housing structure.

# BIM-Based Modular Housing System

## Overview

A BIM-based modular housing system is disclosed, constructed using thin-wall inward-flanging C-section steel or combined square steel as its primary structural elements. This system integrates Building Information Modeling (BIM) technology with prefabricated steel components to deliver an efficient, standardized, and structurally sound approach to modular construction. The design emphasizes rapid assembly, secure connections, and reliable long-term performance.

## Structural Components and Connectors

The system employs three distinct types of connectors to join its core structural elements—foundations, columns, beams, and roof components:

- **Base connectors** are used to link the foundation to the vertical structural members, providing a stable anchoring point for the entire assembly.
- **Butting connectors** facilitate the end-to-end joining of components such as columns and beams, ensuring continuous load transfer along the structural members.
- **Crossed connectors** enable the intersection of horizontal and vertical elements, allowing beams, columns, and roof components to be joined at junction points.

These connectors work in concert to create a cohesive structural framework, tying together the foundation, columns, beams, and roof into a unified system.

## Connection Mechanism and Design Innovation

A key feature of the design is its method of achieving quick and secure butting between components. This is accomplished through the incorporation of **relief holes**, which create an internal-external nesting effect. As components are brought together, the relief holes allow one element to nest within or around another, forming a tight, interlocking fit that enhances alignment and stability during assembly.

To further reinforce these connections, the system utilizes **positioning grooves** that are fastened by steel strips. These grooves guide the components into their correct positions, while the steel strips secure the joint firmly in place. This combination ensures precise alignment and prevents unwanted movement between connected parts.

## Performance Benefits

Through the integration of relief holes, positioning grooves, and steel strip fastening, the system delivers **high-strength joints** with several practical advantages. The nesting effect and secure fastening provide effective connection strength, while the positioning grooves and steel strips work together to prevent slippage between components. The result is a robust, reliable modular housing system that combines the speed and efficiency of prefabricated construction with the structural integrity required for durable, long-lasting buildings.

# Building Information Modeling (BIM) in Modern Construction

The construction industry has undergone a significant transformation over the past few decades, and one of the most influential innovations driving this change is Building Information Modeling, commonly known as BIM. This technology has revolutionized the way architects, engineers, and construction professionals design, plan, and manage building projects.

According to industry experts, BIM is far more than just three-dimensional modeling software. It represents a comprehensive digital approach that integrates every aspect of a building's lifecycle into a single, coordinated system. The model contains detailed information about materials, dimensions, costs, schedules, and even the environmental performance of a structure, allowing stakeholders to make informed decisions at every stage of development.

The primary advantage of BIM lies in its ability to enhance collaboration among different teams. According to numerous case studies, projects that implement BIM effectively experience fewer errors, reduced costs, and shorter completion times. When all parties work from the same digital model, miscommunication is minimized, and potential conflicts can be identified and resolved before construction even begins.

The environmental benefits of BIM should not be overlooked either. According to sustainability reports, the technology enables architects to analyze energy consumption and optimize designs for greater efficiency. This capability supports the growing demand for green buildings and sustainable construction practices worldwide.

As the demand for smarter, faster, and more sustainable construction continues to grow, BIM is expected to become an industry standard. According to forecasts from leading research firms, the adoption of BIM will keep expanding, making it an essential skill for the next generation of construction professionals.

# Abstract

The present invention discloses a Building Information Modeling (BIM)-based modular house constructed using thin-wall channel steel, addressing limitations of conventional prefabricated structures including complex assembly, poor dimensional accuracy, and material inefficiency. The modular house comprises a plurality of standardized structural modules including floor frame assemblies, wall frame assemblies, and roof frame assemblies, each fabricated from cold-formed thin-wall channel steel members to achieve a lightweight yet high-strength load-bearing system.

The structural components include vertical channel steel studs, horizontal top and bottom tracks, and diagonal bracing members, which are interconnected to form rigid rectangular framing units. Adjacent channel steel members are joined through a combination of self-drilling screws, bolted gusset plate connections, and pre-punched slotted holes that facilitate rapid alignment and fastening. Inter-module connections are established via corner connecting brackets and edge splice plates, enabling secure horizontal and vertical coupling of modules into a unified structural assembly.

A BIM platform is integrated throughout the design, fabrication, and construction workflow, wherein a three-dimensional parametric model defines the precise geometry, dimensions, and connection details of each channel steel component and module. The BIM model enables automated generation of fabrication data, clash detection, quantity takeoff, and assembly sequencing, thereby improving construction accuracy, reducing material waste, and shortening the construction period.

The disclosed modular house offers advantages including reduced structural weight, enhanced seismic performance, standardized and repeatable manufacturing, on-site rapid assembly, and disassembly for reuse, making it particularly suitable for residential, temporary, and emergency housing applications.

# Technical Solution Summary: Modular Housing Using Inward-Flanging C-Section and Combined Square Steel

## Core Structural Components

**Inward-Flanging C-Section Steel**
The invention utilizes C-shaped steel profiles featuring inward-turned flanges (lips) at the open edges. This design enhances:
- Sectional rigidity and load-bearing capacity
- Resistance to local buckling
- Concealment of raw edges for cleaner assembly interfaces

**Combined Square Steel**
Square (box) steel members are formed by combining/pairing profiles—often two C-sections joined back-to-back or interlocked—to create closed rectangular sections that serve as:
- Primary columns/posts
- Load-transfer members at critical structural points

## Joint and Connector System

**Column-to-Beam Connections**
- The combined square steel columns connect to C-section beams through **specialized connector plates or brackets**
- Connectors are typically bolted rather than welded on-site, enabling **modular assembly and disassembly**

**Inter-Module Connectors**
- Adjacent housing modules are linked via **corner connectors or joint fittings** that align and secure stacked or side-by-side units
- These transfer both vertical (gravity) and horizontal (wind/seismic) loads between modules

**Flange-Based Interlocking**
- The inward flanges provide engagement surfaces where connecting plates seat and bolt through, distributing stress across the section
- This avoids point loads and improves connection stiffness

## Key Technical Advantages

| Feature | Benefit |
|---------|---------|
| Bolted modular joints | Rapid on-site assembly; reusable |
| Combined square columns | Higher axial capacity from standardized parts |
| Inward flanging | Improved strength-to-weight; safer edges |
| Standardized connectors | Interchangeability and manufacturing efficiency |

---

**Note:** This is a generalized summary based on the described component types. If you have the **specific patent document, application number, or detailed claims**, I can provide a more precise and accurate summary of that particular invention's unique features and connector geometry.

counterfactuals.output:
# Patent Disclosure: Modular Steel Building Connection System

## Field of the Invention

The present invention relates to modular steel building construction, and more particularly to a system of interconnecting structural connectors that enable the rapid assembly and disassembly of columns, beams, walls, and roof plates into a rigid, load-bearing framework.

## Background

Conventional modular steel buildings often rely on welded joints or proprietary fasteners that require skilled labor, extended assembly times, and permanent connections that hinder reconfiguration. There exists a need for a standardized connector system that permits repeatable, high-strength mechanical connections between primary structural members while accommodating modular expansion in horizontal and vertical directions.

## Summary of the Invention

The disclosed connection system comprises three principal connector types—**base connectors**, **butting connectors**, and **crossed connectors**—which cooperate to join columns, beams, walls, and roof plates. Each connector provides standardized interface geometry (e.g., bolt-hole patterns, keyed seats, or flanged faces) that mates with corresponding features on the structural members, thereby transferring axial, shear, and moment loads throughout the assembled structure.

## Detailed Description

### 1. Base Connectors

The **base connector** establishes the foundational interface between a vertical column and an underlying support surface, such as a concrete footing, foundation slab, or lower-story module.

- **Structure:** Each base connector includes a horizontal baseplate having anchor apertures for securing the connector to the foundation, and an upwardly projecting seat or socket dimensioned to receive the lower end of a steel column.
- **Column Engagement:** The lower terminus of the column is inserted into, or bolted against, the seat of the base connector. Fasteners passing through aligned apertures in the column wall and the connector seat fix the column in a vertical orientation.
- **Load Transfer:** The base connector distributes vertical (axial) loads from the column into the foundation while resisting overturning moments and lateral shear through the anchored baseplate.

### 2. Butting Connectors

The **butting connector** joins two structural members that meet end-to-end or in a linear (co-planar) relationship—for example, connecting a beam to a column face, joining adjacent wall panels, or splicing two roof plates along a common edge.

- **Structure:** The butting connector comprises a body having two opposed connection faces oriented to abut the mating ends of the members being joined. Each face carries a pattern of apertures, tabs, or flanges corresponding to the profile of the member.
- **Beam-to-Column Engagement:** A beam terminating at a column is secured by positioning its end against one face of the butting connector, while the opposing face engages the column. Bolts inserted transversely through the connector and the members create a moment-resisting butt joint.
- **Wall and Roof Engagement:** Adjacent wall panels or roof plates are aligned edge-to-edge, and the butting connector spans the interface, clamping or bolting the members to form a continuous, sealed plane.
- **Load Transfer:** The butting connector transmits axial and shear forces across the joint and, depending on aperture arrangement, provides bending resistance sufficient for rigid-frame behavior.

### 3. Crossed Connectors

The **crossed connector** joins structural members that intersect at an angle, typically orthogonally, and that meet from multiple directions at a single node—for example, at a column where beams arrive from two or more horizontal directions, or where roof plates and walls converge at a corner.

- **Structure:** The crossed connector defines a multi-directional body having three or more connection faces arranged along intersecting axes (e.g., an X, T, or L configuration). Each face presents standardized fastening features to receive a respective member.
- **Multi-Member Engagement:** At an intermediate column, for instance, a first beam engages a first face, a second beam engages a perpendicular face, and the column itself may pass through or terminate within a central socket of the crossed connector. This enables simultaneous connection of columns and beams in orthogonal planes at a common joint.
- **Corner and Junction Engagement:** Where a wall, roof plate, and column meet, the crossed connector aligns and secures each member in its respective plane, forming a rigid three-dimensional corner node.
- **Load Transfer:** By tying multiple members into a single node, the crossed connector distributes loads among converging members and maintains the geometric integrity and stiffness of the overall frame.

## Cooperative Assembly

In a preferred embodiment, the connectors are deployed in cooperation as follows:

1. **Base connectors** are anchored to the foundation and receive the lower ends of columns, establishing the vertical framework.
2. **Crossed connectors** are positioned at column-to-beam intersections and at multi-directional junctions to join beams and additional columns in horizontal and vertical planes.
3. **Butting connectors** join beams to columns in linear runs, splice adjacent wall panels, and connect roof plates along their edges.
4. Walls are mounted between columns and beams, and roof plates are secured across upper beams using butting and crossed connectors as dictated by their positions.

Because each connector presents standardized interface geometry, the members and connectors may be prefabricated off-site and assembled on-site using mechanical fasteners alone, without field welding. The mechanical nature of the connections further permits disassembly and reconfiguration of the modular building.

## Advantages

- Rapid, tool-based assembly without skilled welding
- Standardized, interchangeable connector interfaces
- Rigid, moment-resisting joints suitable for multi-story construction
- Modular expandability in both horizontal and vertical directions
- Reusability and reconfigurability of structural components

---

*Note: The foregoing description is illustrative. Specific connector geometries, fastener types, and aperture patterns may be varied within the scope of the invention. For filing, this disclosure should be reviewed by a registered patent attorney or agent and supported by drawings (e.g., FIG. 1 showing the base connector, FIG. 2 the butting connector, FIG. 3 the crossed connector, and FIG. 4 an assembled framework).*

# Building Information Modeling (BIM) Modular Housing System

## System Overview

A BIM-integrated modular housing system combines digital design intelligence with prefabricated construction components to create scalable, repeatable, and precisely-fitted building structures. The system relies on standardized modular units that are designed, tested, and coordinated in a virtual BIM environment before physical fabrication, ensuring that interlocking mechanisms function flawlessly during on-site assembly.

The three critical mechanical features—**relief holes**, **positioning grooves**, and **fastening steel strips**—work in concert to achieve both accurate nesting (proper module alignment) and slippage prevention (resistance to lateral and vertical displacement).

---

## Core Architectural Components

### 1. Modular Unit Structure
Each modular unit is a self-contained volumetric box comprising:
- **Structural frame:** Steel or engineered timber load-bearing skeleton
- **Floor and ceiling cassettes:** Prefabricated horizontal panels
- **Wall panels:** Insulated composite panels with integrated services
- **Connection interfaces:** Standardized edges containing the nesting and locking features

### 2. BIM Coordination Layer
The digital model maintains:
- Parametric definitions of every joint and interface
- Clash detection to prevent geometric conflicts
- Tolerance mapping (typically ±2–3 mm) for fabrication
- Sequencing data for assembly logistics

---

## Interlocking Mechanism: Detailed Function

### Relief Holes

**Purpose:** Relief holes are precision-drilled or cast openings located at the connection faces of each module. They serve multiple functions:

- **Stress dissipation:** They relieve concentrated loads at connection points, preventing material fatigue and cracking around fasteners.
- **Tolerance accommodation:** Slightly oversized relief holes allow for minor dimensional variances during on-site assembly, absorbing the accumulated tolerances of stacked modules.
- **Fastener guidance:** They act as receiving channels that funnel bolts, pins, or locking elements into their correct seated positions.

**Nesting contribution:** As one module is lowered onto another, the relief holes align with corresponding features on the adjacent unit, creating a self-centering effect that draws the modules into their intended relationship.

---

### Positioning Grooves

**Purpose:** Positioning grooves are continuous or segmented channels machined into the mating surfaces of modules (typically along the top and bottom edges of walls and floor slabs).

**How they achieve nesting:**
- **Male-female engagement:** A raised tongue or ridge on one module fits into the corresponding groove on the mating module, similar to a mortise-and-tenon or tongue-and-groove joint.
- **Directional constraint:** The groove geometry physically restricts lateral movement in one or more axes, ensuring modules cannot drift sideways once seated.
- **Progressive alignment:** As modules approach one another, the tapered lead-in of the groove guides misaligned components gently into perfect registration.

**How they prevent slippage:**
- Once the tongue is fully seated within the groove, it creates a **mechanical interlock** that resists horizontal shear forces (from wind loads, seismic activity, or occupancy loads).
- The groove walls provide continuous bearing surfaces that distribute lateral loads across the entire joint length rather than at isolated points.

---

### Fastening Steel Strips

**Purpose:** Fastening steel strips are flat, high-tensile metal bands or plates that bridge across the joint between modules, mechanically tying them together.

**How they work with the other features:**

1. **Seating phase:** After the positioning grooves guide the modules into alignment and the relief holes accept the locating pins, the steel strips are installed across the seam.

2. **Fastening phase:** The strips are bolted through the relief holes into embedded anchor points within each module. Because the relief holes are pre-aligned by the nesting geometry, the bolts pass cleanly through both modules.

3. **Tensioning phase:** As the bolts are torqued, the steel strips clamp the modules together with a controlled pre-load, converting the assembly into a monolithic, rigid unit.

**Slippage prevention through combined action:**
- The **positioning grooves** resist sliding in the horizontal plane.
- The **relief holes** locate the fasteners and absorb tolerances so the connection remains stress-free.
- The **fastening steel strips** apply clamping tension that generates friction across the mating surfaces and resists uplift (vertical separation) and rotational movement.

Together, these three features create a **three-way constraint**: vertical (clamping), horizontal (grooves), and rotational (strip geometry and multiple fastening points).

---

## Assembly Sequence

1. **Digital pre-check:** BIM verifies all module dimensions, joint tolerances, and clash-free geometry.
2. **Foundation preparation:** Base modules are set with positioning grooves facing upward.
3. **Module placement:** Each subsequent module is craned into place; the tapered grooves and relief holes self-align the unit.
4. **Pin engagement:** Locating pins drop through relief holes to establish initial registration.
5. **Groove seating:** Tongues fully engage grooves, locking lateral position.
6. **Strip installation:** Steel strips are laid across seams and bolted through relief holes.
7. **Torquing:** Bolts are tightened to specification, clamping the assembly.
8. **As-built verification:** Sensors or laser scanning confirm alignment matches the BIM model.

---

## Benefits of the Integrated System

| Feature | Nesting Benefit | Slippage Prevention Benefit |
|---------|----------------|----------------------------|
| Relief Holes | Self-centering fastener guidance | Absorbs stress, maintains fastener integrity |
| Positioning Grooves | Progressive tapered alignment | Mechanical resistance to lateral shear |
| Fastening Steel Strips | Bridges and unifies modules | Clamping force resists uplift and rotation |

### Overall Advantages
- **Speed:** Self-aligning features dramatically reduce on-site adjustment time.
- **Precision:** BIM coordination ensures features match perfectly before fabrication.
- **Structural integrity:** The multi-directional locking creates robust, code-compliant connections.
- **Repeatability:** Standardized interfaces allow modules to be mass-produced and freely combined.
- **Reversibility:** Bolted steel strips permit disassembly and reconfiguration for future adaptability.

---

## Conclusion

This BIM modular housing system demonstrates how digital design intelligence and mechanical engineering combine to produce buildings that assemble quickly yet perform reliably. The synergy of relief holes, positioning grooves, and fastening steel strips ensures that each module nests precisely into its neighbors and remains locked against slippage under all service loads—delivering a construction method that is fast, accurate, durable, and adaptable.

# Present Disclosure

The present disclosure relates to the field of prefabricated building structures, and more particularly to a prefabricated thin-wall channel steel housing that enables quick and secure butting of C-section steel members while ensuring enhanced joint strength.

In view of the deficiencies existing in the prior art, wherein conventional thin-wall channel steel connections often suffer from time-consuming assembly procedures, misalignment during on-site installation, and insufficient structural rigidity at the butt joints, the present disclosure aims to provide a prefabricated thin-wall channel steel housing that overcomes the aforementioned drawbacks.

To achieve the above objectives, the present disclosure provides a prefabricated thin-wall channel steel housing comprising a plurality of C-section steel members configured to be butt-jointed with one another. Each C-section steel member is provided at its end with a mating structure that cooperates with a corresponding mating structure of an adjacent C-section steel member, such that the two members can be rapidly aligned and positioned during assembly. A reinforcing connection assembly is disposed at the butt-joint region, the reinforcing connection assembly being configured to clamp, fasten, and structurally bond the abutting ends of the C-section steel members together, thereby forming a rigid and load-bearing joint.

According to the present disclosure, the mating structures are configured to guide the C-section steel members into a predetermined relative position automatically upon engagement, thereby eliminating the need for repeated measurement and adjustment and substantially reducing the on-site assembly time. Furthermore, the reinforcing connection assembly distributes stress across the butt-joint region and increases the effective cross-sectional area at the joint, so as to significantly improve the tensile, shear, and bending resistance of the connection.

By virtue of the above technical solution, the present disclosure achieves quick and secure butting of the C-section steel members, ensures precise alignment and reliable positioning during installation, and provides a joint of enhanced strength and durability. The prefabricated thin-wall channel steel housing thus offers the advantages of high assembly efficiency, superior structural integrity, and improved overall stability, making it particularly suitable for rapid construction of lightweight steel structure buildings.
